candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — laboratory monitoring for medication toxicity
candidate.educational_objective: Monitor serum liver tests before starting valproic acid and at frequent intervals thereafter, with particular vigilance during the first 6 months because of the boxed hepatotoxicity warning.

options.A: Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone before each dose
options.B: Serum liver tests before therapy and at frequent intervals afterward, especially during the first 6 months
options.C: Serum potassium weekly regardless of the client's other medications or conditions
options.D: No laboratory monitoring is needed unless jaundice develops

candidate.rationale: The current valproic acid boxed warning states that fatal hepatotoxicity has occurred, usually during the first 6 months of treatment, and directs clinicians to perform serum liver tests before therapy and at frequent intervals afterward, especially during those first 6 months. Therefore B is correct. A and C are not the label-specified hepatotoxicity monitoring requirement, and D incorrectly delays monitoring until clinical liver injury is apparent.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Valproate-associated fatal hepatotoxicity usually occurs during the first 6 months; serum liver tests should be performed before therapy and at frequent intervals thereafter, especially during the first 6 months.
